meta.fxNote: Cambodia is effectively dollarized. US dollars are the working currency for rent, salaries, visas, and most retail; Cambodian riel is used mainly as small change at roughly 4,000 KHR to US$1. This removes an entire category of currency friction that Vietnam has, and it is one of the genuine practical advantages of moving here. Note the flip side: worn, torn, or pre-2009 US notes are routinely refused.
meta.tagline: The easiest country in the region to stay in legally, and the one where that is changing fastest. Every route, with the 2026 enforcement shift built in.

realityCheck.claim: An apostille will work for my documents, like it does everywhere else.
realityCheck.reality: No. Cambodia is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so an apostille is not accepted. US documents need the full three-step chain: Secretary of State certification for state-issued documents, then US Department of State authentication, then legalization by the Cambodian Embassy. This is the single most expensive misunderstanding on this list, because getting an apostille feels like doing it right.
realityCheck.why: Most countries joined the Convention and most guidance is written for them. Vietnam itself joined with effect from 11 September 2026, which makes the contrast even more confusing for anyone comparing the two.

realityCheck.claim: The business visa lets me work.
realityCheck.reality: It does not. Cambodia runs a two-document system: the EB extension from the Ministry of Interior gives you the right to stay, and a separate work permit from the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training gives you the right to work. Holding EB while working without a permit is illegal employment, and 2026 has brought more frequent compliance checks at businesses and substantial fines.
realityCheck.why: It is called a business visa, everyone calls it a business visa, and for years nobody checked.

realityCheck.claim: Cambodia is the place where you just show up forever and nobody asks questions.
realityCheck.reality: That was substantially true and is becoming less so. The ordinary E-class visa really is extendable indefinitely, which is genuinely rare. But in 2026 extensions increasingly require real supporting documents — employment proof, company papers, accommodation records — and twelve-month extensions require a sponsor. The mechanism is still the most permissive in the region; the paperwork behind it is no longer optional.
realityCheck.why: The reputation was earned over fifteen years and reputations lag reality by several years.

realityCheck.claim: I can buy land or a house in Cambodia.
realityCheck.reality: Foreigners cannot own land. You can own a condominium unit under a strata title, but only on the first floor or above, and only within a cap of 70% of the units in that building. For landed property the routes are a long-term lease, a Cambodian-majority company, or a licensed trustee under the 2019 Trust Law. Nominee arrangements — putting the land in a Cambodian friend's name — are common, and they are exactly as risky as they sound.
realityCheck.why: Property is marketed hard to foreigners, and the distinction between a strata-titled condo and everything else is not something a sales agent volunteers.

realityCheck.claim: Cambodia doesn't tax foreign income, so I'm free and clear.
realityCheck.reality: This is genuinely disputed, and this guide will not pretend otherwise. Professional sources state that residents — anyone present more than 182 days — are taxed on worldwide salary at progressive rates up to 20%. Other sources describe a system that in practice reaches only Cambodian-sourced income. See the contested-claims section: the law and the enforcement pattern point in different directions, and the honest answer is that you are choosing which risk to accept.
realityCheck.why: Both descriptions are repeated confidently by people who have never been assessed either way.

realityCheck.claim: Citizenship by investment is a $245,000 fast track and basically a formality.
realityCheck.reality: The program is real, unlike Vietnam's much-hyped golden visa — but the headline number is not the cost. A US$245,000 donation to the government or a US$305,000 qualifying investment is the entry ticket; all-in costs including fees run to roughly US$330,000 or more per applicant, and you must travel to Cambodia three times during the process. The regulatory framework is also actively evolving.
realityCheck.why: Citizenship-by-investment marketing quotes the donation and omits the fees, exactly as property marketing quotes the unit price and omits the taxes.

nodes.question: How long do you need to stay, and will you be doing any kind of work while you are there?
nodes.help: Cambodia splits sharply at the thirty-day line, and again at the question of work. Getting the entry visa class right at the airport is the cheapest decision you will ever make here, and the most annoying one to undo.

answers.label: Thirty days or less, pure tourism
answers.note: The tourist visa is fine and cheaper.

answers.label: Longer than thirty days, or any kind of work at all
answers.note: Then you want the ordinary E-class visa on arrival, not the tourist one. Keep going.

nodes.question: What will your basis for staying be?
nodes.help: In Cambodia the visa you arrive on is almost always the same — the ordinary E-class — and what differs is the extension you convert it into. So this question is really: which extension class are you aiming at?

answers.label: I am 55 or older and retired, living on a pension or savings
answers.note: Cambodia has a real retirement extension, unlike Vietnam.

answers.label: I have, or expect to have, a Cambodian employer
I will register and run my own Cambodian company
I am enrolling in a Cambodian school or university
I work remotely for foreign clients, or I am job-hunting on the ground
I want Cambodian citizenship and can invest several hundred thousand dollars
I want permanent residence or citizenship, but without a large investment
I genuinely do not know yet — I want to arrive legally and decide there
answers.note: A completely reasonable answer in Cambodia, and one the system actually accommodates.

nodes.question: Three things have to be true at once. Are they?
nodes.help: You need to be 55 or older, able to evidence retirement income or savings, and genuinely not working in Cambodia. The ER extension does not come with the right to work, and taking a local job on it is the same illegal-employment exposure as anything else.

answers.label: Yes — 55 or over, retired, with income I can document, and not planning to work locally
I am 55 or over but I do intend to work in Cambodia
answers.note: Then your route is employment, not retirement — and it needs a work permit.

answers.label: I am under 55
answers.note: The retirement extension is closed to you. The extension classes that are not age-gated are where to look.

nodes.verdict: There is no reliable residence-years-to-citizenship pipeline in Cambodia of the kind that exists in Europe or North America. Ordinary naturalization exists in law, but it is opaque in practice and is not something you can plan a decade around. What Cambodia actually offers is indefinite renewable temporary stay — which is unusually generous, and which is not the same as permanence. If you need a second passport or secure permanent status, the investment route is the only route with a published process.
alternatives: Accept indefinite renewable extensions for what they are: the most permissive long-stay regime in the region, renewed annually, forever. Many long-term foreign residents in Cambodia live exactly this way.
Take the investment route if a passport is genuinely the objective and the cost is bearable — it is a real program with a published process, unlike some regional equivalents.
Marriage to a Cambodian citizen changes the picture and has its own naturalization provisions. If that applies to you, take specific advice; this guide does not cover it in depth.
If permanence is the actual requirement, compare Cambodia against countries that publish a residency-to-citizenship timeline before committing years here.

pathways.name: Tourist (T-class) Visa
pathways.summary: Thirty days, extendable once by thirty days, then you must leave. Cheaper than the ordinary visa and a dead end by design. Correct for a holiday, wrong for anything else.
pathways.bestFor: Genuine tourism of under two months, with no intention to return long-term.
pathways.renewable: No — a single 30-day extension, then exit.

eligibility.requirement: US passport valid at least 6 months with a blank page
eligibility.detail: Standard across all Cambodian visa classes.

eligibility.requirement: Passport photo
eligibility.detail: Bring physical photos as well as digital — on-arrival counters still ask for paper.

costs.item: Tourist visa on arrival or e-visa
costs.note: Confirm the current figure on the official portal; on-arrival and online prices differ slightly.

pathways.timeline: On arrival at the counter, or roughly 3 business days for the e-visa.

steps.title: Decide honestly whether you are a tourist
steps.detail: If there is any chance you will stay past two months, buy the ordinary E-class visa instead. The price difference is about five dollars and it is the difference between a dead end and an open door.

steps.title: Apply online or on arrival
steps.detail: The official e-visa portal is a government site. As in Vietnam, search results are full of resellers.

steps.title: Extend once if you need to, then leave
steps.detail: A single 30-day extension is available. After that the class is exhausted.

verification.check: The current tourist visa fee and whether your nationality can get it on arrival
verification.how: Open the official e-visa portal directly and read the fee and eligibility page before booking flights.
verification.expectAnswer: A published fee on a .gov.kh domain. Any site charging a large 'service fee' on top is a reseller.

failureModes.mistake: Taking the tourist visa to save a few dollars, then deciding to stay
failureModes.consequence: You must exit the country and re-enter on an ordinary visa. A flight and two days lost, for a five-dollar saving.
failureModes.avoid: If in any doubt, take the ordinary E-class visa. It is the single most consequential five dollars in this guide.

failureModes.mistake: Assuming the tourist visa extends indefinitely like the ordinary one
failureModes.consequence: Overstay, at a daily fine, plus an exit problem.
failureModes.avoid: One extension only. Diarise the exit date on arrival.

all.because: the tourist class extends exactly once, then you must leave

pathways.name: Ordinary (E-class) Visa — the gateway
pathways.summary: The most useful document in Cambodian immigration and the reason people call this the easiest country in the region. Thirty days on arrival, and then — uniquely — convertible into an extension of stay that can be renewed indefinitely. Almost every long-term route in this guide starts here.
pathways.bestFor: Everyone staying beyond a month, including people who have not yet decided what they are doing.
pathways.durationGranted: 30 days on entry, then converted to an EB, EG, ER, or ES extension of 1, 3, 6, or 12 months
pathways.leadsToPermanentResidence: No — indefinite temporary stay is not permanence. See the dead end on that question.
pathways.canBringFamily: Each person needs their own visa and extension, including children.
pathways.canWorkLocally: The visa and extension give the right to stay. Work requires a separate work permit.

eligibility.requirement: US passport valid at least 6 months
Ask for the ordinary or business visa at the counter, not the tourist one
eligibility.detail: They are different classes at different prices and the counter will issue whichever you ask for.

costs.note: Five dollars more than the tourist visa, and the only version that leads anywhere.
Requires a sponsor, and increasingly requires real supporting documents.

pathways.timeline: Immediate on arrival. Extensions take a few business days, and are usually handled through an agent.

steps.title: Ask for the ordinary visa at the airport counter
steps.detail: Say 'ordinary visa' or 'business visa', not 'tourist visa'. This is the whole decision.

steps.title: Work out which extension class you qualify for before day 25
steps.detail: EB for business and employment, EG while job-hunting, ER for retirement, ES for study. The class determines what documents you need.
steps.blocker: Do this in your first two weeks, not your last two days.

steps.title: Apply for the extension before the 30 days expire
steps.detail: Most people use an agent; the immigration office also handles it directly. Have accommodation details and supporting documents ready.

verification.check: That the ordinary E-class visa is still being issued on arrival at your entry point
verification.how: Check the official portal's visa-on-arrival page for your intended airport or land border, and confirm the class list includes the ordinary visa.
verification.expectAnswer: The ordinary or business class listed by name, with a fee. Land borders sometimes differ from airports.

verification.check: What supporting documents your chosen extension class currently requires
verification.authority: General Department of Immigration, or a reputable local visa agent
verification.how: Ask specifically: 'For a twelve-month EB extension in 2026, what supporting documents do you require from me and from my sponsor?'
verification.expectAnswer: A concrete document list. Enforcement tightened in 2026, so an answer from 2023 forums is not reliable.

failureModes.mistake: Being given a tourist visa because you did not specify
failureModes.consequence: You are on the dead-end class and will have to exit and re-enter.
failureModes.avoid: Say the words 'ordinary visa' at the counter and check the sticker before you walk away.

failureModes.mistake: Leaving the extension to the last few days
failureModes.consequence: Rushed agent fees, or an overstay if documents are missing.
failureModes.avoid: Start the extension at around day 20.

criteria.note: Open to essentially everyone — this is the gateway visa, and almost every long-stay route in Cambodia starts here.

pathways.name: EB Extension plus Work Permit — employed
pathways.summary: The standard route for anyone working for a Cambodian employer. Two documents from two ministries: the EB extension to stay, and the work permit to work. Both are required, and the calendar around them is unforgiving in a way that catches almost everyone once.
pathways.bestFor: Anyone with a Cambodian employer, including local offices of foreign organisations, schools, and NGOs.
pathways.durationGranted: EB extension up to 12 months; work permit valid to 31 December of the year of issue
pathways.renewable: Yes, annually — but inside a fixed renewal window, not on your own anniversary.
pathways.canBringFamily: Dependants extend on the EB class, sponsored by the same employer.
pathways.canWorkLocally: Yes, with the work permit. The EB extension alone is not work authorisation.

eligibility.requirement: A Cambodian employer to sponsor both documents
eligibility.detail: The employer files the work permit; you cannot obtain one on your own behalf as an employee.

eligibility.requirement: Your employer holds a Foreign Manpower Quota for the year
eligibility.detail: Companies apply for the quota between 1 September and 30 November for the following year, capped at 10% of the Cambodian workforce. If your employer missed that window, your permit cannot be issued no matter how qualified you are.

eligibility.requirement: Passport, recent patent tax certificate from the employer, health certificate, and a 4x6cm photo
eligibility.detail: The health check is done in Cambodia. The patent tax certificate is the employer's, not yours.

eligibility.requirement: Legalized supporting documents where required
eligibility.detail: Degrees and background documents need the full three-step consular chain, not an apostille.

costs.note: Usually paid by the employer. Confirm on the FWCMS portal at application time.
Per document set, including embassy fees and courier. Materially more than an apostille would cost.

pathways.timeline: Work permits run on an annual cycle rather than a per-person one. Realistically 4 to 10 weeks from arrival to both documents in hand, dominated by US document legalization if any is needed.

steps.title: Before accepting the job, ask about the quota
steps.detail: Ask the employer directly whether they hold a Foreign Manpower Quota for the current year with room on it. This one question prevents the worst outcome on this pathway.
steps.blocker: Everything depends on this and it cannot be fixed mid-year.

steps.title: Enter on the ordinary E-class visa
steps.detail: Not the tourist visa.

steps.title: Convert to the EB extension
steps.detail: Your employer sponsors it. Twelve months is the usual target.

steps.title: Complete the health check in Cambodia
steps.detail: Quick and inexpensive, at a recognised clinic.

steps.title: Employer files the work permit on FWCMS
steps.detail: All work permit and employment card applications run through the Foreign Workers Centralized Management System.

steps.title: Diarise the renewal window immediately
steps.detail: Permits are valid to 31 December regardless of when they were issued, and renewals are filed between 1 January and 31 March. Put both dates in your calendar the day you receive the permit.
steps.takes: Two minutes now, saves the year

verification.check: That your employer holds a current Foreign Manpower Quota with capacity
verification.authority: Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training, via your employer's FWCMS account
verification.how: Ask HR to open their FWCMS account and show you the quota for the current year and how many places remain. Ask before you sign anything.
verification.expectAnswer: A number of approved places and a number used. 'We'll sort it out' means they may not have applied in the September-to-November window.

verification.check: The exact work permit renewal deadline for the coming year
verification.authority: Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training
verification.how: Confirm on the FWCMS portal that the renewal window is still 1 January to 31 March, and whether the permit expiry is still fixed at 31 December.
verification.expectAnswer: Published dates. These are administrative deadlines that can move between years, so check annually rather than assuming.

verification.check: Which of your US documents actually need legalization
verification.authority: Royal Embassy of Cambodia in Washington DC, and your employer
verification.how: Ask the employer which documents the labour ministry is requiring this year, then ask the embassy what the current legalization fee and turnaround is for that set.
verification.expectAnswer: A document list from the employer and a fee schedule from the embassy. Do not order legalization for documents nobody asked for.

failureModes.mistake: Joining an employer with no Foreign Manpower Quota
failureModes.consequence: You cannot be issued a work permit at all this year. Either you work illegally or you wait until the next quota cycle.
failureModes.avoid: Ask before signing. This is the highest-value question on this entire pathway.

failureModes.mistake: Assuming the work permit runs twelve months from issue
failureModes.consequence: A permit issued in October expires on 31 December, ten weeks later, and you file a renewal in January having barely used it.
failureModes.avoid: Understand that the permit year is a calendar year, not a personal one.

failureModes.mistake: Missing the 31 March renewal deadline
failureModes.consequence: Penalties, and a period working without a valid permit during a year of increased compliance checks.
failureModes.avoid: Calendar it in January, not March.

failureModes.mistake: Getting an apostille instead of consular legalization
failureModes.consequence: Documents rejected outright; four to eight weeks lost and the fees are not recoverable.
failureModes.avoid: Cambodia is not in the Apostille Convention. Three-step chain, every time.

all.because: the work permit is filed by a registered Cambodian entity

criteria.note: The binding constraint is usually the employer's Foreign Manpower Quota, applied for a year in advance. Ask before signing.

pathways.name: Own Company plus Self-Sponsored EB
pathways.summary: Register a Cambodian company, and it becomes the sponsor for your own extension and work permit. Cambodia's company formation thresholds are far lower than Vietnam's investor tiers, which makes this the realistic self-directed route in the region — at the cost of real, permanent compliance obligations.
pathways.bestFor: Consultants, small business owners, and remote workers who want a clean legal basis and are willing to run a real entity to get it.
pathways.durationGranted: EB extension up to 12 months, renewable indefinitely
pathways.renewable: Yes, while the company remains compliant and the patent tax is current.
pathways.canBringFamily: Dependants extend on the EB class sponsored by your company.
pathways.canWorkLocally: Yes, with a work permit sponsored by your own company.

eligibility.requirement: A registered Cambodian company in good standing
eligibility.detail: With a current patent tax certificate — that certificate is a required document for the work permit application.

eligibility.requirement: A Foreign Manpower Quota for your own company
eligibility.detail: The quota rule applies to your company too. Apply in the 1 September to 30 November window for the following year.

eligibility.requirement: Ongoing monthly and annual tax filings
eligibility.detail: A Cambodian company files whether or not it trades. This is the real cost of the pathway and it never stops.

costs.note: Varies widely by provider and structure. Get more than one quote.
Scales with declared turnover band. Required annually and required for the work permit.
The cost people forget when comparing this against Vietnam's investor route.

costs.amount: About US$400 to 500 per year combined

pathways.timeline: 6 to 12 weeks to a registered company, then the normal EB and work permit cycle on top.

steps.title: Decide whether you want a company or only want a visa
steps.detail: If the answer is only a visa, price three years of accounting and filings before proceeding. A dormant company is a recurring bill and a recurring obligation.
steps.blocker: Make this decision before spending anything.

steps.title: Register the company and obtain the patent tax certificate
steps.detail: The patent tax certificate is what the work permit application actually needs.

steps.title: Apply for your company's Foreign Manpower Quota in the correct window
steps.detail: 1 September to 30 November, for the following calendar year. Miss it and you cannot sponsor yourself next year.

steps.title: Sponsor your own EB extension and work permit
steps.detail: Same FWCMS process as any employer.

steps.title: Set up real bookkeeping from month one
steps.detail: Retrospective bookkeeping in Cambodia is expensive and unpleasant. Start correctly.

verification.check: The genuine all-in annual running cost of the company, not the formation quote
verification.authority: Two or three Cambodian corporate service providers, independently
verification.how: Ask each for a written annual figure covering patent tax, monthly filings, annual return, and audit if applicable. Compare the three.
verification.expectAnswer: Three comparable annual figures. A provider who will only quote formation is quoting you the cheap half.

verification.check: That a company of your size can obtain a Foreign Manpower Quota covering its own foreign director
verification.authority: Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training
verification.how: Ask your provider to confirm how the 10%-of-Cambodian-workforce cap is applied to a company whose only foreign worker is its owner, and what minimum local headcount that implies.
verification.expectAnswer: A concrete answer about local headcount. This is the detail that decides whether a one-person company works.

failureModes.mistake: Forming the company without checking the quota arithmetic for a one-person business
failureModes.consequence: A registered company that cannot lawfully sponsor its own owner.
failureModes.avoid: Run the verification step above before registering, not after.

failureModes.mistake: Treating the company as a visa product and ignoring the filings
failureModes.consequence: Penalties accumulate quietly, and the patent tax certificate you need for the work permit becomes unobtainable.
failureModes.avoid: Budget annual compliance from day one and pay it like rent.

failureModes.mistake: Missing the September-to-November quota window
failureModes.consequence: No work permit next year, from your own company.
failureModes.avoid: It is an annual calendar item. Set it the day you incorporate.

all.because: company formation plus first-year compliance runs to a few thousand dollars — far below Vietnam's investor thresholds

criteria.note: Cambodia has no capital tier for residency, unlike Vietnam. The real cost is permanent annual compliance, not the formation fee.

pathways.name: ER Retirement Extension
pathways.summary: A genuine retirement route, which most of Cambodia's neighbours in this guide do not offer. Age 55 and over, evidence of retirement income, no local work. Renewable indefinitely in 1, 3, 6, or 12-month blocks.
pathways.bestFor: Americans 55 and over living on Social Security, a pension, or savings, who want a low-cost base with genuinely simple paperwork.
pathways.canBringFamily: A spouse generally extends on a dependant basis. Confirm the class for your circumstances.
pathways.canWorkLocally: No. The ER extension carries no right to work, and taking local work on it is illegal employment.

eligibility.requirement: Aged 55 or older
eligibility.detail: The core gate. Exceptional cases are sometimes described, but plan on the age rule.

eligibility.requirement: Evidence you can support yourself without local employment
eligibility.detail: Pension statements, a Social Security benefit letter, or bank statements showing regular deposits. Commonly cited benchmarks sit around US$1,500 per month, but Cambodia does not publish an official minimum the way some neighbours do — see the contested claims section.

eligibility.requirement: Evidence you are retired and not employed
eligibility.detail: A pension statement or Social Security entitlement letter usually serves both purposes.

eligibility.requirement: Entry on the ordinary E-class visa
eligibility.detail: You enter on the ordinary visa and convert. You do not arrive on a retirement visa.

costs.note: Widely used and genuinely useful for this class, given how little official written guidance exists.

pathways.timeline: A few weeks from arrival, most of which is assembling income evidence.

steps.title: Assemble income evidence before you fly
steps.detail: A Social Security benefit letter, recent pension statements, and several months of bank statements. Get them in the US where obtaining them is easy.
steps.blocker: Far easier to obtain before you leave than after.

steps.title: Enter on the ordinary E-class visa
steps.detail: Ask for the ordinary visa at the counter.

steps.title: Apply to convert to the ER extension
steps.detail: Through the immigration office or a local agent, within your first 30 days.

steps.title: Renew before expiry, indefinitely
steps.detail: Twelve months at a time is usual once established.

verification.check: What income evidence the immigration office is actually accepting this year, and whether any minimum figure is applied
verification.authority: Cambodian General Department of Immigration, or the Cambodian embassy in Washington DC before you travel
verification.how: Ask: 'For an ER extension in 2026, what documents do you accept as proof of retirement income, and is there a minimum monthly figure?' Take the answer in writing if you can.
verification.expectAnswer: A document list. If they decline to state a minimum figure, that is itself the answer — see the contested section — and you should over-evidence rather than aim at a rumoured threshold.

verification.check: Whether your spouse can extend alongside you and on what class
verification.how: Ask specifically about a spouse under 55, since the age gate applies to the ER holder.
verification.expectAnswer: A named extension class for the spouse. Do not assume it is automatic.

failureModes.mistake: Arriving on the tourist visa
failureModes.consequence: You cannot convert to ER and must exit and re-enter.
failureModes.avoid: Ordinary E-class at the counter, always.

failureModes.mistake: Taking casual local work — teaching a few hours, helping at a friend's bar
failureModes.consequence: Illegal employment during a year of increased compliance checks, with your extension class contradicting your activity.
failureModes.avoid: If you want to work, you want the EB and work permit route instead, whatever your age.

failureModes.mistake: Aiming exactly at a rumoured income threshold
failureModes.consequence: Refusal, because no official figure is published and the assessment is discretionary.
failureModes.avoid: Over-evidence. Bring more documentation than you think is needed.

all.because: the ER extension is age-gated at 55
you must evidence that you are retired and not working locally

criteria.note: No official minimum income is published, so over-evidence rather than aiming at a rumoured threshold.

pathways.name: EG Extension — job seekers and remote workers
pathways.summary: The extension class for people who are not yet employed. Short EG extensions of 1 and 3 months do not require a sponsor, which makes this the most accessible long-stay mechanism in the region — and the closest thing Cambodia has to a remote worker route, with an important legal caveat.
pathways.bestFor: Job hunters on the ground, people deciding whether to commit to Cambodia, and remote workers who understand the caveat below.
pathways.durationGranted: 1, 3, or 6 months; 12-month extensions require a sponsor
pathways.renewable: Yes in practice, though repeated renewal without ever taking employment attracts more questions than it used to.
pathways.canWorkLocally: No. EG is a permission to stay while seeking work, not to work. Whether it covers remote work for foreign clients is genuinely contested — read the contested section before relying on it.

eligibility.requirement: Entry on the ordinary E-class visa
For 1 and 3-month extensions, no sponsor required
eligibility.detail: This is the unusual feature. Longer extensions require a Cambodian employer or a locally registered company.

eligibility.requirement: For 12-month extensions, a sponsor
eligibility.detail: Either an employer or a registered company. Umbrella arrangements through agents exist and vary in quality and legality — treat them with care.

costs.amount: About US$285 to 300, plus whatever a sponsor costs

steps.title: Enter on the ordinary E-class visa
steps.detail: As always, not the tourist class.

steps.title: Take a short EG extension while you establish yourself
steps.detail: One or three months, no sponsor needed. This buys you time to find either a job or a clearer basis.

steps.title: Decide within that window what your real basis will be
steps.detail: EG is a bridge, not a destination. Employment, your own company, or retirement if you qualify.
steps.blocker: Do not drift on repeated short extensions for years without deciding.

steps.title: Read the contested claim on remote work before relying on EG for it
steps.detail: This is the specific point where Cambodia's reputation for permissiveness and its actual law diverge.

verification.check: Whether short EG extensions are still being granted without a sponsor
verification.authority: General Department of Immigration, or two independent local visa agents
verification.how: Ask two agents separately: 'Can I get a one-month and a three-month EG extension in 2026 with no sponsor, and what documents do you need from me?' Compare the answers.
verification.expectAnswer: Consistent answers from both. Divergence means the practice is shifting and you should assume the stricter version.

verification.check: Whether working remotely for foreign clients requires a Cambodian work permit
verification.authority: Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training
verification.how: Ask whether a foreign national residing in Cambodia and performing services solely for clients outside Cambodia, paid outside Cambodia, requires a work permit.
verification.expectAnswer: Probably not a clean answer — which is exactly why this is in the contested section. Record whatever you are told and who told you.

failureModes.mistake: Treating EG as a de facto digital nomad visa with no further thought
failureModes.consequence: You may be working without a permit, in a year when compliance checks have increased.
failureModes.avoid: Read the contested claim, decide deliberately, and revisit it as enforcement changes.

failureModes.mistake: Buying a 12-month sponsored extension from an agent without asking who the sponsor is
failureModes.consequence: Your legal status depends on a company you have never seen, which may not be compliant itself.
failureModes.avoid: If you are being sponsored, know exactly which registered entity is sponsoring you.

failureModes.mistake: Rolling short EG extensions for years
failureModes.consequence: Increasing scrutiny at each renewal, and no accumulated status to show for the time.
failureModes.avoid: Use EG as a bridge with a decision date attached.

all.because: EG permits you to stay while seeking work, not to work

criteria.note: Short 1 and 3-month EG extensions need no sponsor, which makes this the most accessible long-stay mechanism in the region — and the closest thing to a remote-worker route. Whether it covers remote work is contested.

pathways.name: ES Student Extension
pathways.summary: For enrolment at a recognised Cambodian institution, including Khmer language programs. Inexpensive, low-friction, and a legitimate way to hold clear status while you work out whether Cambodia is right for you.
pathways.bestFor: Younger movers, language learners, and anyone who wants an unambiguous basis for a first year.
pathways.durationGranted: Aligned to the program, in the usual 1, 3, 6, or 12-month extension blocks
pathways.canBringFamily: Limited. Do not plan a family move around this class.

eligibility.requirement: Enrolment at a recognised institution
eligibility.detail: Universities and established language schools. Ask the school directly whether they sponsor ES extensions and how many they did last year.

eligibility.requirement: Entry on the ordinary E-class visa

costs.amount: Same schedule as other extensions, about US$80 for 3 months to US$285 for 12

steps.title: Confirm the school can sponsor before paying tuition
steps.detail: This is the whole risk on this pathway.

steps.title: Enter on the ordinary E-class visa
steps.detail: Ask for the ordinary or business visa at the counter, never the tourist class — the ES conversion needs it.

steps.title: Convert to the ES extension with the school's enrolment documents
steps.detail: Bring the school’s enrolment letter and your accommodation details. Do this inside your first 30 days.

verification.check: That the school actually sponsors ES extensions
verification.authority: The institution, and the General Department of Immigration
verification.how: Ask the school how many ES extensions they supported in the past year and ask to speak to a current foreign student. Then confirm with immigration that the school is recognised for this purpose.
verification.expectAnswer: A number and a student contact. Vagueness means they expect you to arrange your own status, in which case you are really on the EG pathway.

failureModes.mistake: Paying a year of tuition to a school that cannot sponsor
failureModes.consequence: Tuition spent and no status gained.
failureModes.avoid: Confirm sponsorship in writing before paying.

failureModes.mistake: Taking paid work on ES status
failureModes.consequence: Illegal employment exposure.
failureModes.avoid: Keep income sources outside Cambodia, or move to the EB and work permit route.

pathways.name: Citizenship by Investment or Donation
pathways.summary: Cambodia runs a real, published citizenship-by-investment program — a meaningful contrast with the regional trend of announcing golden visas that never launch. It is expensive, it is faster than most, and the headline figure is not the real cost.
pathways.bestFor: People for whom a second passport, not merely residence, is the actual objective, and for whom roughly a third of a million dollars is a considered expense.
pathways.leadsToPermanentResidence: It is the only published route in this guide that leads to permanence.
pathways.canBringFamily: Family applications are contemplated; costs are per applicant and add up quickly.

eligibility.requirement: Donation of US$245,000 to the government, or a qualifying investment of at least US$305,000
eligibility.detail: All-in costs including fees are commonly reported at roughly US$330,000 or more per applicant.

eligibility.requirement: Aged 18 or over with no criminal record
Three visits to Cambodia during the process
eligibility.detail: For documentation, government submission, and passport collection. There is no prior residency requirement.

costs.amount: Frequently bringing the all-in total to US$330,000+
costs.note: Get a written all-in figure before committing to anything.

pathways.timeline: Commonly reported at 3 to 6 months from submission to passport.

steps.title: Get a written all-in quote, not the headline figure
steps.detail: Donation or investment amount, government fees, agent fees, legal fees, translation and legalization, and travel. One number.
steps.blocker: Do not proceed on a headline number.

steps.title: Verify the current legal basis independently
steps.detail: The framework is actively evolving. Confirm the instrument and the current thresholds before transferring funds.
steps.who: You, with independent counsel not paid by the agent

steps.title: Understand the US tax consequences before acquiring a second nationality
steps.detail: Acquiring another citizenship does not end US tax obligations. Take US tax advice first.

steps.title: Complete the three required visits
steps.detail: For documentation, government submission, and passport collection. Plan them into your calendar and budget; there is no prior residency requirement but the visits are not optional.

verification.check: The current legal instrument, thresholds, and whether the program is open today
verification.authority: Independent Cambodian counsel you retain directly — not the agent selling you the program
verification.how: Ask them to name the law or sub-decree the program operates under and confirm the current donation and investment figures in writing.
verification.expectAnswer: A named instrument and current figures. An adviser who cannot name the instrument is not advising you, they are selling to you.

verification.check: Whether all-in costs match what the agent quoted
verification.authority: A second, unaffiliated agent or law firm
verification.how: Get a competing written quote for the identical outcome and compare line by line.
verification.expectAnswer: Two comparable quotes. Large divergence is a reason to slow down, not to pick the cheaper.

failureModes.mistake: Budgeting the headline donation figure
failureModes.consequence: A shortfall of US$85,000 or more against the real all-in cost, discovered mid-process.
failureModes.avoid: Written all-in quote, before anything.

failureModes.mistake: Relying entirely on the agent selling the program
failureModes.consequence: No independent check on an evolving legal framework, with a third of a million dollars committed.
failureModes.avoid: Retain your own counsel. On a purchase this size the fee is rounding.

failureModes.mistake: Assuming a second passport reduces US tax obligations
failureModes.consequence: It does not. US citizens are taxed on worldwide income regardless of other nationalities held.
failureModes.avoid: Take US tax advice before, not after.

all.because: the US$245,000 donation is the entry ticket; all-in costs commonly reach US$330,000 or more per applicant

criteria.note: The only published route to permanence anywhere in this catalogue.

modules.title: Decide and pressure-test
modules.intro: Cambodia's low barrier to entry cuts both ways: it is easy to arrive and easy to drift. Decide what you are doing before you land.

items.task: Run the decision tree and write down your extension class
items.detail: EB, EG, ER, or ES. Everything downstream follows from it.

items.task: Scout on an ordinary E-class visa, not a tourist visa
items.detail: Even for a two-week look, the ordinary visa costs about five dollars more and keeps every door open.
items.why: Buying the wrong class is the most common and most avoidable mistake here.

items.task: Compare Phnom Penh, Siem Reap, and Kampot honestly
items.detail: They differ enormously in cost, medical access, and foreign community. Medical access should weigh heavily if you are over 55.

items.task: Price serious medical evacuation cover
items.detail: Cambodian tertiary care is limited and complex cases are routinely evacuated to Bangkok. Check the evacuation limit, not the headline maximum.

items.task: If retiring, confirm you can document your income before you commit
items.detail: Getting Social Security letters and pension statements is far easier from inside the US.

items.task: Write down what would make you leave
items.detail: Decide now, while you are calm.

modules.title: Assemble and legalize documents
modules.intro: The single biggest difference from most other countries: Cambodia does not accept apostilles. Read this before you order anything.

items.task: Do not get an apostille
items.detail: Cambodia is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention. US documents need the three-step chain: Secretary of State certification for state-issued documents, then US Department of State authentication, then Cambodian Embassy legalization.
items.why: An apostille is the intuitive choice, it feels like doing it properly, and it will be rejected outright.

items.task: Confirm which documents actually need legalizing before paying for any
items.detail: Ask your employer or school for the specific list. Legalizing documents nobody asked for is pure waste at US$200 to 600 a set.

items.task: Have multi-page documents bound correctly
items.detail: The Cambodian Embassy requires multi-page documents to be securely bound with a paging or embossed seal. Incorrect binding is an instant rejection, and the document comes back for redoing.

items.task: Budget six to ten weeks for the full chain
items.detail: Three sequential authorities, each with its own queue and courier legs between them.

items.task: Order extra certified copies
items.detail: Two or three of everything. Reordering from Cambodia is slow.

items.task: Scan everything, including the legalization certificates
items.detail: Full colour, to encrypted cloud storage, before shipping or carrying.

modules.title: Close out the United States
modules.intro: Identical in structure to any US departure, with one Cambodia-specific tax question you must settle yourself.

items.task: Understand you keep filing US taxes forever
items.detail: The US taxes citizens on worldwide income wherever they live.

items.task: Learn the FEIE and FTC basics
items.detail: For tax year 2026 the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion tops out at US$132,900 per person on Form 2555, requiring either the Physical Presence Test of 330 full days abroad or the Bona Fide Residence Test. Earned income only.

items.task: Check the IRS treaty table for Cambodia yourself
items.detail: Do not take anyone's word, including this guide's, on treaty status. Open the IRS list of US income tax treaties and look for Cambodia. If it is absent, there is no treaty relief and no tie-breaker rules, and your defence is FEIE and the Foreign Tax Credit alone.
items.why: Treaty status is the sort of fact that a guide can get stale on and that you can verify in sixty seconds.

items.task: Plan FBAR compliance
items.detail: FinCEN Form 114 is required if your foreign accounts together exceeded US$10,000 at any point in the year. Filed free on the BSA E-Filing system.

items.task: Decide your state domicile deliberately
items.detail: Driver's licence, voter registration, and mailing address as one coherent decision.

items.task: Set up mail forwarding with scanning
items.detail: A real street address, not a PO box.

items.task: Tell your banks and brokerages before you go
items.detail: Some close accounts on a foreign address. Find out while you can still visit a branch.

items.task: Understand Medicare does not cover you in Cambodia
items.detail: And that Cambodian tertiary care is limited enough that evacuation cover is not optional.

items.task: Confirm Social Security payment arrangements abroad
items.detail: Especially important on the retirement pathway, where the benefit letter is also your visa evidence.

items.task: Register for absentee voting
items.detail: Through the Federal Voting Assistance Program.

modules.title: Money and banking
modules.intro: The good news: Cambodia is dollarized, which removes most of the currency friction of a move to Asia.

items.task: Understand that US dollars are the working currency
items.detail: Rent, salaries, visa fees, and most retail are priced in dollars. Riel is used as small change at roughly 4,000 to the dollar.
items.why: This eliminates the exchange-rate exposure that dominates budgeting in most destinations.

items.task: Bring clean, new US notes
items.detail: Torn, marked, or older-series notes are routinely refused, including by banks. This surprises every American once.

items.task: Keep a US bank account open permanently
items.detail: For tax refunds, brokerage links, and US card payments.

items.task: Get cards with no foreign transaction fee before leaving
items.detail: And expect meaningful per-withdrawal ATM fees in Cambodia.

items.task: Open a Cambodian account once you have status and an address
items.detail: Straightforward with an extension and a lease.

items.task: Budget the company's true annual compliance cost
items.detail: Patent tax, monthly filings, and accounting continue whether or not the company trades.

modules.title: Arrival week
modules.intro: One decision at the airport counter shapes everything that follows.

items.task: Ask for the ordinary or business visa, not the tourist visa
items.detail: Say the words, and check the sticker before you leave the counter.

items.task: Photograph your visa sticker and entry stamp
items.detail: The entry date starts both your 30-day clock and your tax-residency count.

items.task: Start counting days toward 182
items.detail: More than 182 days in the calendar year makes you a Cambodian tax resident. See the contested section on what that actually means for your income.

dayCounter.label: You reach 182 days in Cambodia and become a tax resident. Read the contested claim on worldwide versus territorial taxation before this date, not after.

items.task: Get a local SIM with your passport
items.detail: Registration matters for banking and government services.

items.task: Do not sign a twelve-month lease in week one
items.detail: Take somewhere short-term first.

items.task: Begin the extension process around day 20
items.detail: Not day 29.

modules.title: First 90 days
modules.intro: Converting arrival into a stable, renewable basis.

items.task: Convert the ordinary visa into your extension class
items.detail: EB, EG, ER, or ES, with the supporting documents that class now requires.

items.task: Complete the health check in Cambodia
items.detail: Required for the work permit. Quick and inexpensive.

items.task: Get the work permit filed on FWCMS
items.detail: Separate from the visa, from a different ministry, and legally required to work. The EB extension alone is not enough.

items.task: Obtain a certificate of residence from your Sangkat
items.detail: The local commune office. Needed for the driving licence and useful for several other processes.

items.task: Convert your US driver's licence at MPWT
items.detail: You need the licence, a translation into English or Khmer if required, your visa or extension, the Sangkat certificate of residence, three 4x6cm photos, and a medical certificate. Note that a US licence converts only to an equivalent class, and classes C, D and E cannot convert to the same class.
items.why: Riding or driving unlicensed voids most insurance after an accident, and road trauma is the largest health risk to foreigners here.

items.task: Buy health insurance with a real evacuation limit
items.detail: Assume complex care means Bangkok.

items.task: Register with the US Embassy
items.detail: Through the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program.

items.task: Do not buy property in your first year
items.detail: Foreigners cannot own land, condo purchases need a strata title, and nominee structures are genuinely risky. Rent first.

modules.title: Staying legal, year after year
modules.intro: Cambodia's annual cycle is unusual: it runs on fixed calendar dates, not on your personal anniversary. This is where people get caught.

items.task: Diarise the work permit calendar the day you receive the permit
items.detail: Permits are valid to 31 December regardless of issue date, and renewals are filed between 1 January and 31 March. A permit issued in October expires ten weeks later.

items.task: Diarise the Foreign Manpower Quota window
items.detail: 1 September to 30 November, for the following year. If you run your own company this is your job; if you are employed, ask HR in September whether it has been filed.

items.task: Renew your extension before expiry
items.detail: Twelve months at a time once established.

items.task: File your US return and FBAR every year
items.detail: Automatic extension to 15 June for expats, but interest runs from April. FBAR is separate.

items.task: Settle your Cambodian tax position deliberately, once
items.detail: Read the contested claim on worldwide versus territorial taxation, then get a written answer from a Cambodian tax adviser for your specific facts. Do not rely on what other foreigners tell you at a bar.

items.task: Keep the company filings current
items.detail: Including the patent tax certificate, which the work permit application depends on.

items.task: Keep a folder a lawyer could pick up cold
items.detail: Entry stamps, every extension, work permits, leases, filings.

modules.title: Contingency and exit
modules.window: Have this before you need it
modules.intro: Written while things are going well.

items.task: Know what happens to your status if you lose your job
items.detail: Your EB extension and work permit are tied to the sponsoring employer. Ask HR what the clock is before you need to know.

items.task: Understand the overstay regime
items.detail: Overstay is resolved by a daily fine and an exit procedure. It is survivable and it leaves a record.

items.task: Keep three months of expenses plus a flight home, liquid
items.detail: Reachable from either country.

items.task: Keep US documents current
items.detail: Passport, and a valid US driver's licence if you might return.

items.task: Write down your fallback extension class
items.detail: If your current basis fails, which node of the tree do you re-enter at? EG is usually the honest answer, and it is a bridge, not a destination.

gotchas.title: An apostille is the wrong document for Cambodia
gotchas.trap: Cambodia is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention. Americans reflexively order an apostille because that is what works nearly everywhere, and it is rejected. The correct chain is Secretary of State certification for state-issued documents, then US Department of State authentication, then Cambodian Embassy legalization.
gotchas.doThis: Order the three-step consular legalization, and budget six to ten weeks and US$200 to 600 per document set. If you are comparing Cambodia against Vietnam, note that Vietnam moved to apostilles on 11 September 2026 and Cambodia did not — the two countries now need different paperwork.

gotchas.title: The five-dollar decision at the airport counter
gotchas.trap: The tourist visa is about US$30 and extends exactly once. The ordinary E-class visa is about US$35 and extends indefinitely into every long-stay class in this guide. The counter issues whichever you ask for, and most arrivals ask for the tourist visa because it is called the tourist visa.
gotchas.doThis: Say 'ordinary visa' or 'business visa' at the counter, and check the sticker before walking away. If you are even slightly unsure how long you will stay, pay the extra five dollars.

gotchas.title: Your work permit expires on 31 December no matter when you got it
gotchas.trap: Work permits run on the calendar year, not on a twelve-month clock from issue. A permit issued in October expires on 31 December, and the renewal is filed between 1 January and 31 March.
gotchas.doThis: The day you receive the permit, put 31 December and 31 March in your calendar. If you are joining an employer late in the year, ask whether it is worth waiting for the new permit year.

gotchas.title: The Foreign Manpower Quota is applied for a year in advance
gotchas.trap: Companies must apply for their Foreign Manpower Quota between 1 September and 30 November for the following year, capped at 10% of their Cambodian workforce. If your prospective employer missed that window, you cannot be issued a work permit that year regardless of your qualifications.
gotchas.doThis: Ask any prospective employer, before signing, whether they hold a current quota with capacity remaining. Ask to see it in their FWCMS account.

gotchas.title: The business visa is not permission to work
gotchas.trap: Cambodia runs two documents from two ministries: the EB extension from the Ministry of Interior for the right to stay, and the work permit from the Ministry of Labour for the right to work. Holding EB while working without a permit is illegal employment, and 2026 has brought more frequent business compliance checks and substantial fines.
gotchas.doThis: Treat them as two separate obligations with two separate deadlines. Never assume the visa agent who got your EB also handled the work permit — ask explicitly.

gotchas.title: Badly bound documents are rejected on sight
gotchas.trap: The Cambodian Embassy requires multi-page documents to be securely bound with a paging seal or embossed seal. A stapled or loose multi-page document is rejected instantly, and you start the chain again.
gotchas.doThis: Confirm binding requirements with the embassy before submitting, and use a legalization service that has done Cambodia specifically rather than a generic apostille shop.

gotchas.title: You cannot own land, and the workarounds carry real risk
gotchas.trap: Foreigners cannot own land in Cambodia. You can own a condominium unit under a strata title, but only above the ground floor and only within a 70% foreign cap per building. For anything landed, the routes are long leases, a Cambodian-majority company, or a licensed trustee. Nominee arrangements — the land in a Cambodian friend's name — remain common and are exactly as risky as they sound.
gotchas.doThis: Rent for at least a year. If you do buy, buy a strata-titled unit and verify the title is registered with the Ministry of Land Management. Get independent counsel who is not connected to the seller or the agent.

gotchas.title: Cambodia's permissiveness is being quietly tightened
gotchas.trap: The country's reputation was built on extensions granted with minimal paperwork. In 2026, extensions increasingly require genuine supporting documents, accommodation records, and in some cases work permit or business proof, and compliance checks at businesses are more frequent.
gotchas.doThis: Do not plan on advice from forum posts more than a year or two old. Verify current requirements with two independent local agents before each renewal, and keep your paperwork genuinely in order rather than nominally.

gotchas.title: Old or damaged US banknotes are refused
gotchas.trap: Cambodia is dollarized, which is a real convenience, but notes that are torn, heavily marked, or from older series are routinely rejected by shops and even banks. Meanwhile change under a dollar comes back in riel.
gotchas.doThis: Bring crisp, recent notes. Inspect notes you are given as change, and refuse damaged ones at the point of transaction rather than discovering the problem later.

gotchas.title: Your US licence may not convert to the class you actually need
gotchas.trap: Conversion at MPWT produces an equivalent class only, and classes C, D and E cannot be converted to the same class. As in much of the region, the practical risk is riding a motorbike on a licence that does not cover it, then discovering after an accident that insurance declines.
gotchas.doThis: Convert your licence properly, obtain the motorbike class if you intend to ride, and get written confirmation from your health and travel insurers that they cover motorbike use at your licence class.

contested.question: Does Cambodia tax a resident's foreign-sourced income?

positions.position: Yes. Residents — anyone present more than 182 days in the tax year — are taxed on worldwide salary income at progressive rates up to 20%, with a foreign tax credit available for tax paid abroad.
positions.heldBy: Professional tax guidance, including major-firm country summaries

positions.position: In practice, no. Cambodia's tax administration focuses almost exclusively on locally registered companies and formal local employment, and foreigners on foreign payrolls are effectively outside the net.
positions.heldBy: Widely repeated expat and nomad tax commentary

contested.practicalEffect: These describe the law and the enforcement pattern respectively, and both are probably accurate descriptions of their own subject. That means you are not choosing between two facts, you are choosing how much enforcement risk to carry. The exposure grows the longer you stay, the more visible your local footprint becomes, and the more the administration modernises.
contested.howToResolve: Get a written opinion from a Cambodian tax adviser for your specific facts — where you are paid, by whom, and for work performed where. Ask specifically whether they would file a return for someone in your position, and what happens if the position is later challenged. This costs a few hundred dollars and is the only way to convert a rumour into a position you can defend.

contested.question: Does working remotely for foreign clients from Cambodia require a Cambodian work permit?

positions.position: Yes, arguably. The work permit regime covers foreigners working in Cambodia, and the labour authorities have not carved out remote work for foreign employers. Work performed physically in Cambodia is work in Cambodia.
positions.heldBy: A conservative reading of the labour regime

positions.position: In practice, no. Enforcement targets businesses employing foreigners locally, and the EG extension exists precisely for people who are in Cambodia without a local employer.
positions.heldBy: Established expat practice and the design of the EG class

contested.practicalEffect: Cambodia is materially more permissive here than Vietnam, but permissiveness is not permission. The 2026 tightening was aimed at businesses rather than individuals, which is why this remains unsettled rather than resolved.
contested.howToResolve: If the risk matters to you, remove it structurally: register a company and sponsor your own work permit, which is far cheaper here than the equivalent in Vietnam. If you accept the risk, at least accept it knowingly, and revisit the question at every renewal.

contested.question: Is there a minimum income requirement for the ER retirement extension?

positions.position: Around US$1,500 per month is the working benchmark, and applicants should evidence at least that.

There is no official published minimum. Cambodia does not publish a figure the way several neighbouring countries do; the requirement is to show you can support yourself without local employment, assessed with discretion.
positions.heldBy: Official and semi-official descriptions of the ER class

contested.practicalEffect: Because the assessment is discretionary rather than arithmetic, aiming precisely at a rumoured threshold is the wrong strategy. More evidence is strictly better, and the form of the evidence matters as much as the amount.
contested.howToResolve: Ask the immigration office or the Cambodian embassy directly what they accept, and bring more documentation than any published figure suggests: benefit letter, pension statements, and several months of bank statements.

watchlist.title: The 2026 tightening of extension and compliance requirements
watchlist.whatChanges: If documentation requirements for extensions keep rising, the EG bridge narrows and Cambodia stops being the region's easy option. The reality check and the EG pathway would both need rewriting.

watchlist.title: Citizenship-by-investment framework and thresholds
watchlist.whatChanges: Thresholds and the governing instrument are described as actively evolving. Any change alters the only permanence route in this pack.

watchlist.title: Work permit renewal window and quota dates for the next cycle
watchlist.whatChanges: The 1 January to 31 March renewal window and the 1 September to 30 November quota window are administrative dates that can move between years. They drive the most consequential deadlines in this pack.

watchlist.title: Tax administration reach over foreign-sourced individual income
watchlist.whatChanges: If the General Department of Taxation begins assessing resident foreigners on foreign-source income, the first contested claim resolves and the money module needs a substantial rewrite.

watchlist.title: Cambodia's position on the Apostille Convention
watchlist.whatChanges: Cambodia remains outside the Convention. Vietnam's accession in September 2026 makes this a live comparison, and any Cambodian move would simplify the documents module considerably.
